376: func (u dashboardUseCases) RunOperation(ctx context.Context, req OperationRequest, emit func(OperationEvent)) (OperationResult, error) {
377: 	expected := req.ExpectedFingerprint
378: 	req.ExpectedFingerprint = ""
379: 	prepared, err := u.PrepareOperation(ctx, req)
380: 	if err != nil {
381: 		return failedOperation(OperationResult{Subject: operationFirstNonEmpty(req.Project+"/"+req.Sprint, req.Study)}, err)
382: 	}
383: 	if expected != "" && expected != prepared.InputFingerprint {
384: 		return failedOperation(OperationResult{Subject: prepared.Subject}, ErrStaleOperation)
385: 	}
386: 	req = prepared.Request
387: 	if emit == nil {
388: 		emit = func(OperationEvent) {}
389: 	}
390: 	emit(OperationEvent{State: OperationRunning, Stage: req.Stage, Message: "operation started"})
391: 	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
392: 		return OperationResult{State: OperationCancelled}, err
393: 	}
394: 	ss := u.sprintService()
395: 	result := OperationResult{State: OperationComplete, Subject: operationFirstNonEmpty(req.Project+"/"+req.Sprint, req.Study)}
396: 	stage := sprint.PlanningStage(req.Stage)
397: 	switch req.Kind {
398: 	case OperationValidate:
399: 		validationReq := ValidationRequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint, Study: req.Study, Stage: req.Stage}
400: 		switch {
401: 		case req.Study != "":
402: 			validationReq.Subject = ValidationStudy
403: 		case req.Sprint != "":
404: 			validationReq.Subject = ValidationSprint
405: 		default:
406: 			validationReq.Subject = ValidationProject
407: 		}
408: 		validation, err := u.Validate(ctx, validationReq)
409: 		if err != nil {
410: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
411: 		}
412: 		result.Message = validation.Status
413: 		result.Findings = append(result.Findings, validation.Findings...)
414: 	case OperationSprintStatus:
415: 		r, err := ss.Status(req.Project, req.Sprint)
416: 		if err != nil {
417: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
418: 		}
419: 		result.Message = summarizeSprintStatus(r)
420: 	case OperationPrompt:
421: 		p, err := promptSprintStage(ss, req.Project, req.Sprint, stage)
422: 		if err != nil {
423: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
424: 		}
425: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(p.Prompt)
426: 	case OperationFlowDryRun:
427: 		r, err := runSprintFlow(ctx, ss, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.FlowRequest{To: stage, DryRun: true})
428: 		if err != nil {
429: 			result = operationWithSprintFindings(result, r.Findings)
430: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
431: 		}
432: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Message)
433: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("flow to %s dry run", stage)
434: 	case OperationStageDryRun:
435: 		r, err := ss.FlowStage(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.FlowRequest{To: stage, DryRun: true})
436: 		if err != nil {
437: 			result = operationWithSprintFindings(result, r.Findings)
438: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
439: 		}
440: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Message)
441: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("single-stage %s dry run", stage)
442: 	case OperationExecuteDryRun:
443: 		r, err := ss.Execute(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.ExecuteRequest{DryRun: true, TaskID: req.Task})
444: 		if err != nil {
445: 			result = operationWithSprintFindings(result, r.Findings)
446: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
447: 		}
448: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Prompt)
449: 		result.Message = r.Message
450: 	case OperationExecuteStatus:
451: 		r, err := ss.Status(req.Project, req.Sprint)
452: 		if err != nil {
453: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
454: 		}
455: 		execute := summarizeExecute(r.ExecuteState)
456: 		if !execute.Available {
457: 			result.Message = execute.Message
458: 		} else {
459: 			result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%d total: %d pending, %d running, %d complete, %d failed, %d cancelled", execute.Total, execute.Pending, execute.Running, execute.Complete, execute.Failed, execute.Cancelled)
460: 		}
461: 	case OperationReviewDryRun:
462: 		r, err := ss.Review(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.ReviewRequest{DryRun: true, Concurrency: req.Parallelism})
463: 		if err != nil {
464: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
465: 		}
466: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(r.Prompt)
467: 		result.Message = r.Message
468: 	case OperationReviewStatus:
469: 		r, err := ss.Status(req.Project, req.Sprint)
470: 		if err != nil {
471: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
472: 		}
473: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s verdict=%s fresh=%t next=%s", r.Verification.Review.ExecutionStatus, r.Verification.Review.Verdict, r.Verification.Review.Fresh, r.Verification.Review.NextAction)
474: 	case OperationSmokeStatus:
475: 		r, err := ss.VerificationStatus(req.Project, req.Sprint)
476: 		if err != nil {
477: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
478: 		}
479: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s verdict=%s fresh=%t run=%s issues=%d assessment=%s next=%s", r.Smoke.ExecutionStatus, r.Smoke.Verdict, r.Smoke.Fresh, r.Smoke.RunID, len(r.Smoke.Issues), r.Assessment, r.NextAction)
480: 	case OperationSmokeDryRun:
481: 		r, err := ss.RunSmoke(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.SmokeRequest{Level: req.Level, Suite: req.Suite, Test: req.Test, ForceReview: req.ForceReview, OverrideConfirmed: req.ForceReview, OverrideRationale: req.OverrideRationale, DryRun: true})
482: 		if err != nil {
483: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
484: 		}
485: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: %s", r.ScopeKind, r.Scope, r.ScopeRationale)
486: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(sprint.RenderSmoke(r))
487: 	case OperationQAStatus:
488: 		qa, err := u.QAStatus(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
489: 		if err != nil {
490: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
491: 		}
492: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("phase=%s fresh=%t shards=%d/%d next=%s", qa.Phase, qa.Fresh, qa.CompletedShards, qa.TotalShards, qa.NextAction)
493: 	case OperationQADryRun:
494: 		qa, err := u.QAMap(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
495: 		if err != nil {
496: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
497: 		}
498: 		data, _ := json.MarshalIndent(qa, "", "  ")
499: 		result.Content, result.Truncated = boundContent(string(data))
500: 		result.Message = "read-only QA map ready"
501: 	case OperationQARecover:
502: 		qa, err := u.RecoverQA(ctx, QARequest{Project: req.Project, Sprint: req.Sprint})
503: 		if err != nil {
504: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
505: 		}
506: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("phase=%s next=%s", qa.Phase, qa.NextAction)
507: 	case OperationVerifyDryRun:
508: 		r, err := ss.Verify(ctx, req.Project, req.Sprint, sprint.VerifyRequest{To: sprint.PlanningStage(req.Stage), DryRun: true, Review: sprint.ReviewRequest{DryRun: true, Focus: req.ReviewFocus, Restart: req.RestartReview}, Smoke: sprint.SmokeRequest{Level: req.Level, Suite: req.Suite, Test: req.Test, ForceReview: req.ForceReview, OverrideConfirmed: req.ForceReview, OverrideRationale: req.OverrideRationale, DryRun: true}})
509: 		if err != nil {
510: 			return failedOperation(result, err)
511: 		}
512: 		result.Message = fmt.Sprintf("assessment=%s next=%s", r.Verification.Assessment, r.Verification.NextAction)
513: 	default:
514: 		if u.runner == nil {
515: 			return failedOperation(result, fmt.Errorf("runtime-backed operation is unavailable without configured composition"))
516: 		}
517: 		return u.runner(ctx, req, emit)
518: 	}
519: 	emit(OperationEvent{State: OperationComplete, Stage: req.Stage, Message: operationFirstNonEmpty(result.Message, "operation complete")})
520: 	return result, nil
521: }

541: func validateOperationScope(req OperationRequest) error {
542: 	for name, value := range map[string]string{"project": req.Project, "sprint": req.Sprint, "study": req.Study} {

544: 			continue
545: 		}

548: 		}
549: 		for _, r := range value {

551: 				continue
552: 			}
553: 			return fmt.Errorf("invalid operation %s reference", name)
554: 		}
555: 	}
556: 	return nil
557: }

559: func normalizedStrings(values []string) []string {
560: 	seen := make(map[string]struct{}, len(values))
561: 	out := make([]string, 0, len(values))
562: 	for _, value := range values {
563: 		value = strings.TrimSpace(value)
564: 		if value == "" {
565: 			continue
566: 		}
567: 		if _, ok := seen[value]; ok {
568: 			continue
569: 		}
570: 		seen[value] = struct{}{}
571: 		out = append(out, value)
572: 	}
573: 	sort.Strings(out)
574: 	return out
575: }

663: func fingerprintOperationInputs(root, canonical string, inputs []string) (string, error) {
664: 	hash := sha256.New()
665: 	_, _ = hash.Write([]byte(canonical))
666: 	for _, rel := range inputs {
667: 		path := filepath.Join(root, filepath.FromSlash(rel))
668: 		info, err := os.Lstat(path)
669: 		if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) {
670: 			continue
671: 		}
672: 		if err != nil {
673: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("inspect governed input %s: %w", rel, err)
674: 		}
675: 		if info.Mode()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
676: 			return "", fmt.Errorf("governed input %s must not be a symbolic link", rel)
677: 		}
678: 		if info.IsDir() {
679: 			var files []string
680: 			if err := filepath.WalkDir(path, func(item string, entry fs.DirEntry, walkErr error) error {
681: 				if walkErr != nil {
682: 					return walkErr
683: 				}
684: 				if entry.Type()&os.ModeSymlink != 0 {
685: 					return fmt.Errorf("governed input %s must not contain symbolic links", rel)
686: 				}
687: 				if !entry.IsDir() {
688: 					files = append(files, item)
689: 				}
690: 				return nil
691: 			}); err != nil {
692: 				return "", fmt.Errorf("scan governed input %s: %w", rel, err)
693: 			}
694: 			sort.Strings(files)
695: 			for _, item := range files {
696: 				itemRel, _ := filepath.Rel(root, item)
697: 				if err := hashOperationFile(hash, item, filepath.ToSlash(itemRel)); err != nil {
698: 					return "", err
699: 				}
700: 			}
701: 			continue
702: 		}
703: 		if err := hashOperationFile(hash, path, rel); err != nil {
704: 			return "", err
705: 		}
706: 	}
707: 	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(hash.Sum(nil)), nil
708: }

710: func hashOperationFile(hash interface{ Write([]byte) (int, error) }, path, rel string) error {
711: 	data, err := os.ReadFile(path)
712: 	if err != nil {
713: 		return fmt.Errorf("read governed input %s: %w", rel, err)
714: 	}
715: 	_, _ = hash.Write([]byte("\x00" + rel + "\x00"))
716: 	_, _ = hash.Write(data)
717: 	return nil
718: }

720: func summarizeSprintStatus(status sprint.StatusSummary) string {
721: 	parts := make([]string, 0, len(status.Stages)+2)
722: 	for _, stage := range status.Stages {
723: 		parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s=%s", stage.Stage, stage.Status))
724: 	}

Findings summary:

**F1 (High confidence, Medium severity): Terminal-persistence failures are demoted from exit 6 to exit 4 on every durable CLI verb; QA contradicts its own documented mapping.**
- `durableCLICommand.Finish` (durable_operations.go:71-84) deliberately classes persistence failure as ExitRuntime(6) (`classifiedCause(ExitRuntime, err, "run-control.finish")`).
- `finishDurableCLICommand` (86-91) joins it into the run error.
- Every handler then re-classifies the joined error through mappers whose default arm is ExitWorkspace(4): flow/verify/execute/review → `mapSprintError` (sprint_commands.go:944-963); smoke → `mapSmokeError`→`mapSprintError`; qa → `mapQACommandError`→`mapSprintError` (662-679); study ×4 → `mapStudyExecutionError` (study_commands.go:950-959). The inner classedError's class is ignored because handlers wrap a NEW classedError; `fail()` (app.go:236-239) reads only the outermost.
- Proven: probe test shows all six verb families return 4 for the exact error shape Finish() produces. cli-reference.md:26 defines 4=workspace/filesystem and 6=runtime/provider; :363 explicitly says QA "runtime or persistence failures 6". Also recovery.md:190 treats persistence failure as its own class of problem.
- Bad outcome: work completed successfully but terminal row unwritten → operator sees exit 4 "workspace/filesystem" and per stableCommandError guidance inspects workspace/validation rather than DB health; automation treating 4 as non-retryable input problem skips the retry that doc semantics for 6 would trigger.
- Additional instance: `qa cancel/run/resume` route pre-work repository-open failures through the same mapper: empirically corrupt `.ultraplan/run-control.db` → `run list`=6, `sprint flow`=6, but `sprint qa run/cancel --json`=4 with envelope `error.code="validation.workspace"` — direct violation of cli-reference.md:363.

**F2 (High confidence, Medium-High severity): substring classification sniffs user-controlled text in flow/execute/review ladders → wrong exit classes.**
- sprint_commands.go:269, 363, 507: `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")`.
- Error messages embed user-controlled project/sprint names and absolute workspace paths (project.RefError.Error() at discovery.go:19-27; fs errors embed full paths).
- End-to-end proof on frozen binary, identical failure ("open .../requirements.md: no such file or directory"), only project name differs:
  - `sprint demo s1 flow --to plan --dry-run` → 4
  - `sprint runtime-demo s1 flow ...` → 6
  - execute: demo→4, runtime-demo→6
  - review: demo→4, runtime-demo→6
  - JSON mode same command/project → 4 (ladder differs by stream!)
- Also RefError path: typed mapper gives 5 for `project reference "runtime-demo" not found`, text ladder gives 6 (probe + code).
- The codebase's own TUI/web classifier (`failedOperation`, operations.go:751-796) refuses to sniff free-form text (guarded by sprint_error_test.go:29-41), so CLI behavior contradicts in-repo doctrine.
- Bad outcome: scripts/agents see "provider/runtime" (transient, retry-later) for deterministic validation/filesystem problems, or vice versa if a message happens to include the word without being runtime-related; JSON vs text divergence breaks consumers that switch modes.

**F3 (Medium confidence of frequent trigger, High confidence of gap): `mapRunControlError` has no cancellation/deadline arms → SIGINT during `run` door DB calls exits 6, and `run follow` can exit 6 despite documented clean-stop.**
- run_commands.go:403-414: only InvalidArgument/NotFound/Conflict/Terminal/default(6). context.Canceled falls to default → ExitRuntime(6). Probe-verified.
- runcontrol passes ctx errors through raw (sqlite.go:1104-1106), so cancellation surfaces mid-call.
- runFollow guards ctx.Done only in the idle-wait select (188-193); Events/Snapshot calls (162-179) run under deps.ctx and return canceled mid-poll — follow polls every 250ms during catch-up and replays up to 512 events per batch, so interrupt-during-query is realistic. Result: exit 6 + stderr noise where doc says "Interrupting follow stops observation only" (:509-511) and where the idle path deliberately returns 0. Every other family maps cancellation distinctly (7, or QA 8).
- Bad outcome: wrappers that treat nonzero as failure/restart signal misread an operator Ctrl-C as a provider/runtime fault.

**F4 (Low-Medium severity, High confidence): `health` reports `filesystem.read: ok` unconditionally — the documented readability check never reads anything.**
- health_commands.go:65 hardcodes Status ok with Message=marker filename; nothing stats/opens the file. Doc cli-reference.md:115 says health checks "filesystem readability".
- Empirical: chmod 000 ultraplan.yml → `config.validation: fail ... permission denied` but `filesystem.read: ok - ultraplan.yml` in the same run (JSON checks array too). Operators/scripts consuming health see a passing check for a property that is false at that moment.

**F5 (Low severity, Medium confidence): `serve` usage errors print 15 lines of help to stdout AND duplicate the error line on stderr.**

# Result: `review-cli-dispatch-exit-contract-adversarial` (fresh-context adversarial review)

Target: ultraplan-go @ 50d6f0d25ff273f4cb956f11e6030376108110bc (exported to /tmp/opencode/cli-review; target repo untouched).
Method: full read of dispatch surface + docs; frozen binary built and executed against crafted workspaces in /tmp/opencode/ws-rt; package-internal probe tests (zz_gauntlet_probe_test.go in the scratch export) exercised the real classifiers. No subagents.

## F1. Durable finish-persistence failures exit 4 instead of 6 on every durable verb; QA violates its own documented mapping

- Claim: `durableCLICommand.Finish` classes terminal-persistence failure as ExitRuntime (`classifiedCause(ExitRuntime, err, "run-control.finish")`, durable_operations.go:80-83), but every handler re-classifies the joined error through mappers whose default arm is ExitWorkspace(4), discarding the inner class (`fail`, app.go:236-239, reads only the outermost classedError).
- Path: `finishDurableCLICommand` joins Finish's error (durable_operations.go:86-91) → flow/verify/execute/review → `mapSprintError` default→4 (sprint_commands.go:944-963); smoke → `mapSmokeError`→`mapSprintError`; qa → `mapQACommandError`→`mapSprintError` (662-679); study run-loop/run-all/run/synthesize → `mapStudyExecutionError` default→4 (study_commands.go:950-959).
- Proof: probe test feeds the exact Finish() error shape through the real mappers — all six families return 4 ("run-control.finish: sqlite: disk I/O error" contains no "runtime" substring, so the substring arms do not rescue it). No test pins this either way.
- Contract: cli-reference.md:26 (`6`: runtime/provider error) vs :25 (`4`: workspace or filesystem error); cli-reference.md:363 explicitly promises "runtime or persistence failures 6" for QA.
- Second instance, empirically reproduced end-to-end: corrupt `.ultraplan/run-control.db` → `run list`=6 and `sprint demo s1 flow --to plan`=6 (begin error returned raw), but `sprint demo s1 qa run --json` and `qa cancel --run x --json` exit 4 with envelope `"error.code":"validation.workspace"` for a persistence failure — direct contradiction of cli-reference.md:363 (sprint_commands.go:402-407, 419-422 route repository/begin errors through mapQACommandError).
- Bad outcome: work completed but terminal row unwritten → operator sees the workspace/filesystem class and `stableCommandError` recovery text ("repair the reported cause" pointing at workspace/validation), not DB health; automation that treats 4 as deterministic-input failure skips the retry semantics class 6 carries. QA consumers additionally get a wrong stable `error.code`.
- Severity: medium. Confidence: high. Regression test: force `FinishOperation` to fail after successful work (inject failing repository) and assert exit 6 / `provider.runtime` per verb family; corrupt-DB test asserting qa exits 6 with code `provider.runtime`.

## F2. Substring classification sniffs user-controlled names/paths: identical failures exit 6 vs 4 depending on project name; JSON and text modes of the same command diverge

- Claim: the flow/execute/review ladders branch on `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` (sprint_commands.go:269, 363, 507). Error messages embed user-controlled refs and absolute paths (`project.RefError.Error()` = ``project reference "<ref>" not found`` , project/discovery.go:19-27; fs errors embed the full workspace path).
- End-to-end proof (frozen binary, only the directory/project name differs, same underlying failure `open .../requirements.md: no such file or directory`):
  - `sprint demo s1 flow --to plan --dry-run` → **4**; `sprint runtime-demo s1 ...` → **6**
  - `execute --dry-run`: demo→**4**, runtime-demo→**6**; `review --dry-run`: demo→**4**, runtime-demo→**6**
  - Same command, same project, JSON mode: runtime-demo → **4** (JSON arm uses mapSprintError, sprint_commands.go:258-263)
  - Probe: typed mapper gives 5 for RefError("runtime-demo"); the text ladder returns 6 for the same error.
  - Control `sprint runtime-demo s2 ...` (sprint-ref error whose message lacks "runtime") → 5, confirming the mechanism is pure substring accident.
- Counter-evidence checked: no doc freezes message wording for these branches; the codebase's own adapter classifier refuses free-form sniffing (`failedOperation`, operations.go:751-796) and is test-guarded for exactly this property (sprint_error_test.go:29-41) — the CLI ladders are separate code without that guard.
- Bad outcome: scripts/agents receive "provider/runtime" (transient-retry semantics) for deterministic validation/filesystem failures whenever a name/path contains "runtime"; mode-switching consumers see different classes for one failure. Also reachable via any workspace path containing "runtime".
- Severity: medium-high (silent, data-dependent contract breakage on the primary automation verbs). Confidence: high. Regression: table-driven tests running flow/execute/review for projects named `x-runtime-y` vs `x-y` asserting equal classes; replace substring checks with typed sentinel/`errors.As` classification.

## F3. `mapRunControlError` has no cancellation/deadline arms: SIGINT during `run` door queries exits 6; `run follow` can exit 6 despite documented clean-stop

- Claim: run_commands.go:403-414 maps only InvalidArgument→2, NotFound→5, Conflict/Terminal→8, default→6. `context.Canceled` falls to default → ExitRuntime(6) (probe-verified). runcontrol passes ctx errors through raw (internal/runcontrol/sqlite.go:1104-1106), so cancellation surfaces mid-call.
- Reachability: `runFollow` guards ctx.Done only in the idle-wait select (run_commands.go:188-193); its `repository.Events`/`Snapshot` calls (162-179) run under the signal context — follow polls every 250ms during catch-up and replays 512-event batches, so an interrupt landing inside a query returns a canceled error mapped to 6 plus a stderr line, while the identical interrupt during idle waits exits 0. Doc: "Interrupting follow stops observation only" (cli-reference.md:509-511). Every sibling mapper classifies cancellation distinctly (7; QA 8).
- Bad outcome: wrappers treating nonzero as fault/restart misread operator Ctrl-C (or shutdown-driven cancellation) as a provider/runtime failure; `follow`'s own two behaviors disagree.
- Severity: medium. Confidence: high on the gap, medium on day-to-day trigger frequency (timing window). Regression: unit test `mapRunControlError(context.Canceled)` == 7 (plus follow integration asserting exit 0 when canceled mid-Events).

## F4. `health` reports `filesystem.read: ok` unconditionally — documented readability check never reads

- health_commands.go:65 hardcodes `Status:"ok"` with the marker filename as message; nothing stats/opens anything. cli-reference.md:115 says health checks "filesystem readability".
- Empirical: `chmod 000 ultraplan.yml` then `ultraplan health` prints `config.validation: fail ... permission denied` alongside `filesystem.read: ok - ultraplan.yml` (same in the `--json` checks array).
- Bad outcome: operators and health-gating scripts see a passing check for a property false at that moment; the check cannot ever fail, so it carries no signal while claiming one.
- Severity: low-medium. Confidence: high. Regression: unreadable-marker-file test asserting `filesystem.read` status != ok (or removal of the fake check).

## F5. `serve` usage errors print full help to stdout and duplicate the diagnostic on stderr

- serve_commands.go:20 sets flag output to stderr and :23 overrides `fs.Usage` to write help to stdout; flag invokes Usage on parse errors too, then `fail()` prints the classified error again (app.go:233). Measured: `ultraplan serve --bogus` → stdout 15 lines of help, stderr 2 lines (`flag provided but not defined: -bogus` + `serve: flag provided but not defined: -bogus`), exit 2.
- Every other verb emits nothing to stdout and one stderr line on usage errors; the surface's own discipline (stdout stays machine-readable; one stderr diagnostic) is broken for the one verb most likely to be wrapped by scripts that capture stdout.
- Severity: low. Confidence: high. Regression: assert empty stdout and single stderr line for `serve --bogus` (route parse-error usage away from stdout).

## Defended / non-issues

- `finishDurableCLICommand(nil, err)` nil-safe for dry-run/prompt/defer paths (durable_operations.go:87-89).
- QA cancellation/deadline → exit 8 (`qa.cancelled`) vs generic 7 asymmetry is explicitly documented (cli-reference.md:363) — intended.
- Empty alias digest making CLI alias-dedup unreachable: no concrete failure found at this layer (dedup is web-owned).
- Study verbs accept before service construction, but `runRepository` loads config before acceptance for all durable verbs, so invalid-config invocations create no runs anywhere.
- `study status --json` label always "ok", `sprint status --json` label "partial" with exit 0: phase3-json-schemas.md:80 satisfied (never interpreted as pass); no contract violated.
- `code --output` writes outside the workspace: no containment promise exists in-tree; CWD-relative resolution is consistent for reports and output.
- DeadlineExceeded→6 in mapSprintError/mapRunControlError matches the class table; verify's zero-value verification block on early failure renders garbage text but never reports success (phase3:78) and exits correctly.
- Existing tests do not pin any of F1-F5 (searched: no finish-failure class pins; flow/execute/review ladder tests use messages that legitimately contain "runtime").

Reproduction artifacts: scratch export `/tmp/opencode/cli-review` (binary + `internal/app/zz_gauntlet_probe_test.go`), workspace fixtures under `/tmp/opencode/ws-rt`. Target repo and planning workspace untouched.

part.text:
Review complete. Findings written to `review/jobs/review-cli-dispatch-exit-contract-adversarial/result.md`. Five defects, all verified against the frozen binary (`50d6f0d`) plus probe tests; none pinned by existing tests.

**F1 — Finish-persistence failures demoted 6→4 (medium, high conf).** `Finish()` classes DB failure as ExitRuntime (durable_operations.go:81), but every handler re-wraps via mappers defaulting to ExitWorkspace(4) (sprint_commands.go:961, study_commands.go:958). Proven for all six verb families. Worse: corrupt run-control DB → `run list`=6 but `sprint qa run/cancel --json`=**4** with envelope code `validation.workspace` — directly contradicting cli-reference.md:363 ("runtime or persistence failures 6").

**F2 — Substring classification sniffs user-controlled names (medium-high, high conf).** `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "runtime")` (sprint_commands.go:269/363/507) matches project names and workspace paths. Empirical, identical failure differing only in name: `sprint demo s1 flow --to plan --dry-run`→**4**, `sprint runtime-demo ...`→**6**; same for execute and review; JSON mode of the same command→4. The TUI/web classifier refuses text-sniffing by design (operations.go:751-796 + sprint_error_test.go guard) — the CLI ladders contradict in-repo doctrine.

**F3 — `mapRunControlError` has no cancellation arm (medium).** SIGINT landing inside a `run *` query exits 6 instead of 7; `run follow` can exit 6 mid-poll despite its documented clean-stop guarantee (idle-path deliberately returns 0 at run_commands.go:188-193). runcontrol passes `context.Canceled` through raw.

**F4 — `health` `filesystem.read: ok` is hardcoded (low-medium).** health_commands.go:65 never reads anything; demoed with chmod-000 config: check reports ok alongside a permission-denied config failure. Doc claims readability checking.

**F5 — `serve` usage errors dump 15 help lines to stdout + duplicate error on stderr (low).** Every other verb emits nothing to stdout on usage errors.

Defended non-issues (QA cancellation→8 asymmetry, empty alias digest, nil durable handling, `--yes` gate ordering, status-label semantics, etc.) are documented in the result file with evidence and repro artifacts under `/tmp/opencode/cli-review` and `/tmp/opencode/ws-rt`. Target repo untouched.
